## Historical audit: S0094

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/replay_s1_r1/M_descendant/C1/replay_development/commons_2238909/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to this file. Only chunk 2 of 3 is visible; image paths are recorded, but the images themselves are not available for this audit.

| Evidence | Observation |
|---|---|
| Goal and first builds — student `model_request`, line 15 [0,191900) | The explicit task was an editable reconstruction of one indoor photograph. The student’s code interpreted it as an archive aisle: architecture, multiple mobile shelving units, a book bay, left furniture and ceiling fixtures. That semantic interpretation and the recorded image anchors are not independently verified here. |
| Revision after step 1 — line 15 [0,191900) | The runner reported step 1 successful. The student claimed the cabinet tops were too high, opening too far left, panels too wide and broad surfaces too bright. It then lowered cabinet and ceiling heights, narrowed and redistributed panels, moved the opening, and reduced illumination while retaining the camera. Step 2 was also reported successful. These are student assessments, not independent image comparisons. |
| Third revision — student `model_response`, line 17 [0,12130); `execute`, line 18 [0,12818) | After receiving step 2’s render, the student claimed convergence and opening position agreed, but tops remained high, panels were too narrow and surfaces too bright. The executed program lowered shelving from 2.60 to 2.47, broadened units, darkened the floor and set exposure to −0.7, retaining camera and ceiling. Geometry and appearance changed together, so their separate effects cannot be established. |
| Scene construction — lines 17 [0,12130), 18 [0,12818) | Code defines many separate objects and colors, shelf contents, cranks and signs under shelving owners, floor noise/bump and diffuser materials. Ownership is evidence of intended part grouping, not proof of physical contact, support or collision-free connections. Upright placements and a fixed camera are coded; reference pose and placement agreement are unverified. Marker-based shader changes are conditional, so their effective application is not demonstrated by the code alone. |
| Validation and selection — `execution_result`, line 19 [0,77464); `select`, lines 20–21 [0,59) each | Step 3 returned `ok: true`, completed a render and saved an image and blend file; step 3 was selected twice. This is **technical execution success**, not demonstrated visual or geometric correctness. Final reconstruction quality remains unknown; no independent functional or visual check is visible. |
| Input and exploration — `model_request`, line 15 [0,191900); `codex_session`, line 16 [0,3920) | The student actually received procedural system instructions and runner review prompts, then produced revisions consistent with those prompts. No distinct teacher diagnosis or teacher-proposed update is identified in this visible chunk, so teacher receipt or adoption cannot be asserted. The recorded third student session had zero tool calls; no autonomous external exploration is evidenced. |

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, successful rendering should be separated from verification of appearance, camera, object support and semantic completeness; simultaneous geometry and lighting changes also confound diagnosis. Task-specific hypotheses concern archive-panel widths, shelving height, opening position and floor brightness. Whether the third revision improved any of them, whether parts actually connect, and whether camera or lighting caused the reported mismatches remain unresolved without the images or independent checks. The unseen chunks may contain additional events; none are inferred here.
